seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

In Connect Four strategy, the central columns (especially column 3) are the highest-value positions because they enable the most potential winning lines (horizontal, vertical, and both diagonals). action.thoughts:
To make the optimal move, analyze the board: only column 3 has pieces (x at row 5, o at row 4), creating a nearly empty board with perfect left-right symmetry. No immediate wins or threats exist (connect-4 required).

Key priorities: control the center, create connected pieces (prioritize chains of 2+), maximize future forks/potential lines (horizontals, verticals, diagonals), and respond to opponent's likely best counter.

- Playing column 3 (row 3 x): Legally stacks x above o, but creates no connection (x-o-x vertically separated; no 2-chain). Opponent can then play column 2 (or 4) at row 5 o, creating their first 2-chain (diagonal: row 5 col 2 o to row 4 col 3 o). Result after opponent response: you have zero 2-chains, opponent has one 2-chain. Suboptimal.
- Playing column 2 (or 4) at row 5 x: Creates immediate 2-chain horizontal (row 5 col 2/4 x adjacent to col 3 x). Opponent's best counter is column 4/2 row 5 o (symmetric block), creating their 2-chain diagonal (row 5 col 4/2 o to row 4 col 3 o). Result: mutual 2-chains (balanced, but yours horizontal low/stronger foundation). Other opponent replies worse for them (e.g., column 3 row 3 o gives you fork: column 4/2 row 5 x makes 3-horizontal threatening both ends; opponent blocks one, you win).
- Edges (0,1,5,6) worse (fewer lines); column 1/5 creates distant singles (no chain).

Columns 2 and 4 tie perfectly (symmetric). Column 2 chosen as tiebreaker (lowest index).

Final Answer: 2
